## When you'd use this

Use an image when a picture helps the respondent: a map of how to find the clinic, as above, a photo of the entrance, or your organisation's logo. An image collects no answer.

## Before you start

- **The image must already be online.** The builder doesn't store image files: you give it the image's address. That is either:
  - an address starting with `https://`, such as `https://example.org/map.png`; or
  - a path on the server of the app your form is used in, starting with a single `/`, such as `/images/logo.png`.
- **Write the alt text before you start:** a sentence that says what the image shows, for respondents who can't see it.
- An image has no Required and no Help text, isn't numbered, and can't be the source of a condition. It can have conditions of its own, under **Logic**.

## Steps

1. Below the last block, select **+** (Insert a block), or type `/` in the line beside it.
2. Under **Media**, choose **Image**. Typing `picture` or `photo` finds it too.
3. In **Label**, write the alt text. As the hint under it says, it is read aloud to screen-reader users, so describe what the image shows. In the example, the label is "Map of the clinic: the entrance faces Main Street, the parking lot is beside the clinic, and reception is just inside the entrance."
4. In **URL**, paste the image's address or path.
5. To add a caption that everyone sees, put a Text block right after the image.
6. Select **Save**.
<Gif alt="Adding an Image with its alt text and URL" />

The example's image is a file on this docs site, so its URL is a path:

<FormExcerpt form="image" block="entrance_map" field="content" />

## What happens behind the scenes

- **The image is shown at its own size, never wider than the form.** On a narrow screen it shrinks to fit.
- **The Label is the image's alt text,** what screen readers announce in its place. There is no separate caption setting.
- **A path starting with `/` loads from the app the form is used in,** not from the builder. If that app runs under a sub-path, its developer can tell the form where, so the path still works.
- **An address that isn't accepted, or an image that fails to load, shows nothing:** never a broken-image icon, and never an error for the respondent.
- **The image loads only when it is about to come into view,** and the image's server isn't told which page it is on.
- **Nothing from an image is sent** with the answers.

## Rules the builder enforces

| What you try | What the builder says |
|---|---|
| Save an image with no URL, or one that isn't accepted | Image "Map": add an image address starting with https:// or a path on your app's server such as /images/logo.png. (under the URL field: Add an image address starting with https:// or a path on your app's server such as /images/logo.png.) |

The name in quotation marks is the image's path in the form: the page and groups it is in, then its label.

What is accepted, after spaces at either end are removed:

| Accepted | Not accepted |
|---|---|
| `https://example.com/a.png` | `http://example.com/a.png`: must be `https://` |
| `HTTPS://example.com/a.png` | `images/a.png`: a path must start with `/` |
| `/images/a.png` | `//cdn.example.com/a.png`: two slashes at the start |
| | `https://user@cdn.example.com/a.png`: a name or password in the address |
| | `data:image/png;base64,…`: images can't be pasted in as data |

## Troubleshooting

**The image doesn't show, though the form saved.** The address was accepted, but the file isn't there: check it opens in a browser. For a path starting with `/`, check it on the app your form is used in, not on the builder.

**The builder refuses an `http://` address.** Only `https://` is accepted. Try the same address with `https://`, or put the image on your app's server and use its path.

**Respondents need to read text that is in the image.** Put that text in the alt text, or in a Text block next to the image, so everyone can read it.
